title: Wrong Level of Abstraction (General Trait with Specific Pollution)
pattern: An interface or trait declares a method that only makes sense for certain concrete implementations, forcing other implementers to either "lie" or return dummy, nonsensical values.
why_bad: It pollutes the clean interface abstraction. A boundless or dynamic stack implementation cannot compute `percent_full()` accurately and is forced to return a default like `0.0`, which is a semantic lie that breaks client assumptions.
detection: A trait method declaration that cannot be logically implemented by all known or planned implementers without using dummy default outputs.
counterexample: Traits where optional capabilities are explicitly represented via `Option` return types that are logically consistent for all implementers.
fix: Refactor the specific method out of the general trait and place it into a specialized sub-trait or concrete struct (e.g., `trait BoundedStack: Stack`).
source: Robert C. Martin, *Clean Code* (2008), Chapter 17, G6 ("Code at Wrong Level of Abstraction").
